sections.title: Algerian regulation has changed direction
body: Law 25-02 of February 2025, amending and supplementing Law 01-19 on waste management, control and disposal, writes the **circular economy** into Algerian law: extended producer responsibility (EPR), eco-design, a digital waste management system and tougher penalties.

For a business the meaning is simple: the waste you generate stays attached to you all the way to its final destination. The question is no longer "who takes it away", but "can you prove where it went".

about.title: About us
about.intro: EL MAIN LIL SINAA — **المعين للصناعة** — supports Algerian businesses on one specific point: moving their waste oil out of the informal circuit and back into a clean, documented, legal cycle.

sections.title: Why we exist
body: Algeria consumes around 180,000 tonnes of lubricants a year and generates up to 110,000 tonnes of waste oil. A large share is neither collected nor tracked: it ends up burned, poured onto the ground or into sewers. A single litre of oil is enough to contaminate an enormous volume of water.
Our job is to make the right move easier than the convenient one: the right container, a fixed collection date, a document in order.

rules.metaTitle: Algerian environmental regulation — EL MAIN LIL SINAA
rules.metaDescription: Overview of Algerian legislation: Law 01-19, Law 25-02, Law 03-10, Executive Decree 13-176, environmental taxes and the SNGID 2035 strategy.
rules.title: Regulation: Algeria's environment from A to Z
rules.intro: The texts governing waste, waste oils and environmental taxation in Algeria, summarised in plain language. **Always check the latest version in the Official Journal (JORADP)** before acting.

items.title: Law 01-19 of 12 December 2001
items.text: Waste management, control and disposal: duty to sort, recover and dispose of waste in environmentally sound conditions.

items.title: Law 25-02 (Official Journal no. 12, February 2025)
items.text: Amends and supplements Law 01-19: extended producer responsibility, eco-design, a digital management system, phase-out of single-use plastics, revised penalties.

items.title: Law 03-10 of 19 July 2003
items.text: Environmental protection for sustainable development: general framework, prevention and polluter-pays principles.

items.title: Executive Decree 13-176 of 30 April 2013
items.text: Conditions for manufacturing, storing and wholesaling lubricants, and for regenerating waste oils (Official Journal no. 25 of 12 May 2013).

items.title: Executive Decree 02-175 of 20 May 2002
items.text: Creation, organisation and operation of the National Waste Agency (AND), under the environment ministry.

items.title: Environmental taxes (Finance Acts)
items.text: Tax on polluting or hazardous activities, tax on oils and lubricants, incentive tax on destocking special industrial waste, plastic bag tax, and supplementary taxes on air pollution and wastewater.

items.title: National Integrated Waste Management Strategy (SNGID)
items.text: By 2035: recover 47 % of municipal waste, cut generation below 1.1 kg per inhabitant per day, eliminate illegal dumps and create 30,000 direct jobs.

items.title: Ministry of the Environment
items.text: Sets national policy and supervises the sector's public bodies.

items.title: AND
items.text: National Waste Agency: flow data, technical support and recycling promotion.

items.title: CNTPP

items.title: ONEDD
items.text: National Observatory for Environment and Sustainable Development: measures and publishes environmental data.

items.title: CNFE
items.text: National Conservatory for Environmental Training: training and awareness for practitioners.

items.title: Wilayas & municipalities

contribution.metaTitle: Eco-contribution and environmental taxation — EL MAIN LIL SINAA
contribution.metaDescription: Understanding Algerian environmental taxes on oils, lubricants and special industrial waste, and the obligations that follow.
contribution.title: Eco-contribution & environmental taxation
contribution.intro: In Algeria the **polluter-pays** principle translates into a set of environmental taxes voted each year in the Finance Act. Here is the practical reading for a business.

items.title: Tax on oils, lubricants and lubricating preparations
items.text: Applies to products whose use generates waste oil. The 2026 Finance Act forecasts DZD 7.5 billion in revenue, split 66 % to the State and 34 % to municipalities.

items.title: Tax on polluting or hazardous activities
items.text: Payable by classified installations, according to their nature and capacity.

items.title: Incentive tax on destocking special industrial waste
items.text: Penalises prolonged on-site storage of special waste. 2026 forecast: DZD 550 million, 84 % to the State and 16 % to municipalities.

items.title: Specific tax on plastic bags
items.text: Applies to bags imported or produced locally.

items.title: Supplementary taxes: air pollution and wastewater
items.text: Based on industrial discharges exceeding regulatory limits.

sections.title: Your obligations, in plain terms
body: Whoever produces waste remains responsible for it until final disposal or recovery. In practice: know what you generate, store it properly, hand it to a licensed operator, and be able to prove it.
That is exactly what we document for you, collection after collection.

faq.metaTitle: Frequently asked questions — EL MAIN LIL SINAA
faq.metaDescription: Answers to common questions about waste oil collection, regulatory compliance and costs in Algeria.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: The questions we get most often, on the phone and on site.

items.q: Can I pour waste oil down the drain or burn it?
items.a: No. Unauthorised discharge and burning are prohibited and carry penalties, strengthened by Law 25-02. Oil must be handed to a licensed operator.
It depends on the stream. Cooking oil in regular volumes can be bought back; small volumes and associated waste involve a charged service. The quote is always in writing.

items.q: What is the minimum volume for a collection?
items.a: We run shared rounds: even a small producer can be added to an existing route.
A transfer note at every visit stating type, quantity and destination, plus an annual summary.

items.q: Do you operate in the South?
items.a: Yes, in industrial and oil zones, at a frequency adapted to the distances. Contact us for your area's schedule.

items.q: Can engine oil and frying oil be mixed?
items.a: Never. Mixing makes the stream unrecoverable and can downgrade everything to hazardous waste. Always two separate containers.

items.q: What happens to the oil collected?
items.a: It goes to recovery: re-refining, energy recovery or biodiesel production, depending on quality and available outlets.
Yes: sealed bins and drums, labelled, delivered and maintained by us.
You present your transfer notes and register. That is precisely what our traceability file is built to cover.
